description: Evidenced inputs for counting business-day commencement clauses. JRH's direction (2026-10-27) is that article 28 of the Ley Federal de Procedimiento Administrativo governs the count. A date is produced only when a text version applies on every counted day AND the suspension and vacation notices for the whole window are evidenced here; a missing notice is never read as no notice. Empty suspension_periods and notice_coverage therefore resolve no clause. Edit only with a recorded decision.

counting_rule.direction: JRH 2026-10-27: article 28 LFPA governs business-day counting for these commencement clauses
counting_rule.reading: the Nth business day after the day of publication; the day of publication is not counted

statute_versions.evidence: The committed article carries no amendment marks and no DOF reform note, and its recorded effective_from is 1995-06-01, so the text is read as unchanged since entry into force. This is the committed record's own evidence; the historical DOF editions were not consulted.

sexennial_holidays.reason: transmission of the Federal Executive, every six years. Evidenced through 2018 only: from 2024 the Executive changes on 1 October (constitutional reform, DOF 10-02-2014), and whether article 28 then excludes 1 October, 1 December or neither is not decided here, so any count reaching 2024, 2030, ... is insufficient (Codex review 2026-10-28, deferred limit 3)
